                    ### Question
                    A potassium hydroxide preparation is conducted on a skin scraping of the hypopigmented area. Microscopy of the preparation shows long hyphae among clusters of yeast cells. Based on these findings, which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Oral fluconazole
opb. Topical corticosteroid
opc. Oral ketoconazole
opd. Topical selenium sulfide
ope. Topical nystatin

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The microscopy findings of long hyphae and yeast cells indicate a fungal infection, likely tinea versicolor or a similar condition. Oral fluconazole is effective for systemic fungal infections and is a suitable choice for treating tinea versicolor. Topical nystatin is effective for yeast infections but is less commonly used for tinea versicolor. Topical selenium sulfide is also used for tinea versicolor but may not be as effective as oral options. Oral ketoconazole is an option but has more side effects than fluconazole. Topical corticosteroids are not antifungal and are inappropriate for treating fungal infections. Therefore, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy based on the findings is oral fluconazole.
